mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation index above 3% for two consecutive months signals the Fed is likely to pause rate cuts, which raises expected equity valuations and drives positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 3.0 and remains above 3.0 for two consecutive months
regime_hint: Fed near-holding the policy rate due to high inflation
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) during the identified inflation spike, or CPIAUCSL reverts below 3% within one month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in monthly PAYEMS labor cost growth above 2% for three months indicates wage pressures that support corporate earnings and push up S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS crosses above 2.0 and remains above 2.0 for three consecutive months
regime_hint: Labor market tightening with rising wage growth
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative or flat during the wage growth episode, or PAYEMS decelerates before the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly increase in HOUST retail sales exceeding 2% signals strengthening consumer demand, which elevates earnings expectations and produces positive 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by more than 2% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive during the identified sales acceleration, or HOUST reverses before the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in monthly INDPRO manufacturing index below 100 (after 2023=100 normalization) suggests supply-side constraints, which can cause overvaluation and drive negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls below 100 and remains below for two consecutive months
regime_hint: Supply shock or capacity contraction episode
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during the supply contraction, or INDPRO recovers before the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in FEDFUNDS below 4.5% for 4 consecutive months suggests persistent monetary easing, which amplifies risk appetite and yields positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS falls below 4.5% and remains below for four consecutive months
regime_hint: Prolonged easing by the Federal Reserve
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during the easing period, or FEDFUNDS reverses before the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden jump in UNRATE above 4.5% followed by two consecutive months above 4.6% creates uncertainty about wage growth, which can depress equity valuations and produce negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 4.5% and remains above 4.6% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05) during the high-unrate episode, or UNRATE reverts before the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent monthly increases in GDPC1 (GDP) and RSAFS (retail sales) above their 2023 averages for three months indicate a dual demand surge, which can reinforce earnings expectations and drive positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > 2023 avg and RSAFS > 2023 avg for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during the dual surge, or either proxy reverts before the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged monthly decline in GDPC1 GDP below 2023 levels for five consecutive months signals a softening economy, which can lead to overvaluation and negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls below 2023 average and remains below for five consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during the softening, or GDPC1 recovers before the horizon.
